extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, corporate communicators, and business leaders (Ragan Insider readers)
extracted.subtask_description: An op-ed examining the communication errors that accelerated Elizabeth Holmes' downfall and the lessons those mistakes hold for PR professionals when managing scrutiny and crisis. Focus is on what not to do in corporate communications and crisis response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management style based on secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing a management style based on secrecy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy in management is identified as a fatal error in corporate communications; the piece implies openness/transparent management is preferable when facing scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignoring employees who voiced concerns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article links ignoring internal concerns to the company's downfall, noting that employees' grievances going public ultimately sealed the company's fate—implying organizations should listen to and address employee concerns proactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antagonizing credible journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Antagonizing credible journalists along the way
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively antagonizing reputable reporters is presented as a PR misstep; maintain constructive relationships with credible journalists rather than hostility, especially under scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceptive marketing / false pretenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing the firm's flawed lab testing technology under false pretenses (duping investors, board members, clients, and journalists)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making false or misleading claims about products/technology is a core ethical and reputational failure; honest, fully disclosed representations are necessary to avoid long-term collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to address internal discontent before it goes public
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal discontent that prompted team members to go public with their grievances is what ultimately took down the company
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unresolved internal problems can become public crises; organizations should resolve internal disputes, provide safe channels for concerns, and act before issues escalate externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor handling of scrutiny (general 'what not to do')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Holmes saga is described as a clinic in 'what not to do' when faced with scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When under scrutiny, avoid secrecy, ignoring staff concerns, antagonizing journalists, and deceptive claims; instead, the implication is to engage transparently, respond constructively to criticism, and correct misinformation.
